competitorFacts.text: ARC Prize named Tufa Labs and its Duck agent the first-place open-source solution for the June 2026 ARC-AGI-3 Milestone 1 prize.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Tufa Labs — Duck Harness technical overview
competitorFacts.text: Tufa Labs says its public Duck harness lets an LLM inspect game grids as image and text, write Python in a REPL, and keep context short by evicting older messages. This describes the published Milestone 1 system, not an unverified current submission.
Tufa Labs lists Dries Smit, Isaiah Pressman and Jeroen Cottaar among its AI researchers, with research interests spanning reinforcement learning, self-play and Bayesian methods.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Tufa Labs — October 9 public competition post
competitorFacts.text: On October 9, 2026, Tufa Labs described a temporary setback in a public X post and said it remained dedicated to crushing competitors with overwhelming resources and compute.
Yi-Chia Chen’s Kaggle profile lists her as a Competitions Master and a double-degree student at National Taiwan University and Waseda University.

discussionThreads.author: huikang
discussionThreads.reason: Newly collected older research background, not a fresh Oct 12 release: source created Oct 1, latest visible reply Oct 6. Body and replies verified in logged-out Chrome at 21:06:55Z. Board reports 18 comments; thread heading counts 15 top-level comments. Useful concrete comparison for Sunday research and future method coverage.
discussionThreads.summary: Tong Hui Kang compares the three Milestone 2 winning ARC-AGI-3 solutions and links their notebooks and write-ups. He describes a shared Duck/TAAF foundation and compares serving, scheduling, context management and harness changes. In the replies, rellik13 says requests waited for cache space despite high decode throughput and describes reallocating memory to longer history. Mintu Kumar asks for request-latency and cache-wait measurements. The desk also read Franzen’s linked write-up, which distinguishes its submission configuration from inherited defaults and says the experiments were not a complete controlled ablation study.

socialPosts.author: OCEANVIN10
socialPosts.summary: OCEAN highlighted the Memento 3 preprint. Its authors report that a fixed language model revises an external rulebook and executable world model; on the 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, they report clearing every level with fewer actions than the human baseline. These are author-reported results on the public set.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A new ARC-AGI-3 research lead for the edition desk. The paper provides a concrete mechanism and results, but the public tutorial set cannot establish private-game performance.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announced Yi-Chia Chen at 59.17% on the 2026 ARC-AGI-3 Kaggle board, taking the lead over Tufa Labs.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A new public-board leader is the strongest ARC-3 standings lead; verify the current board before an edition.

socialPosts.author: guanningzeng
socialPosts.summary: Zeng links the Schema preprint, public implementation repository and project site, and credits the research team. The repository was read without sign-in.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Direct primary-source links for reporters. Code was inspected as source material, not run or installed.

socialPosts.author: guanningzeng
socialPosts.summary: In an author-reported ten-public-game ablation, removing executable modeling, history checks, planning or runtime verification reduces performance.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Explains the design claim; grouped with the release rather than a separate score story.

socialPosts.author: guanningzeng
socialPosts.summary: Zeng reports that Schema with Claude Fable 5 clears the 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games and improves relative human action efficiency over Claude Code. The paper supports this author-reported public-set comparison.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Useful technical context for the release; the public tutorial set does not establish competition performance.

socialPosts.author: guanningzeng
socialPosts.summary: Zeng announces Schema’s full report and code, building on its July public-game demonstration. The linked preprint was submitted September 30; this is an October 12 release announcement.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A fresh release lead with publicly accessible paper and implementation. Public-game evaluation; no private Kaggle result established.

socialPosts.author: crysis44k
socialPosts.summary: English translation of the Japanese post: fshindo thinks local LLM enthusiasts with many GPUs who improve harnesses and inference speed ought to enter competitions, then jokes about discovering formidable people who would become rivals. This is a friendly invitation, not a claim about a named rival’s resources.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Japanese competitor voice about the connection between practical inference/harness work and contest participation.

socialPosts.author: cunkpyber
socialPosts.summary: PunkCyber tells the ARC Daily Digest that 復活の混テキスト is their team. The exact Japanese name matches entries on the current ARC-3 and ARC-2 boards; these have separate competition team IDs.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A competitor checked in with the paper and supplied a direct team identification. It supports a friendly shout-out; the reply does not identify their individual Kaggle handle or establish who produced a submission.

socialPosts.author: crysis44k
socialPosts.summary: Posting in Japanese, fshindo said the ARC-AGI-3 competition had taught them a great deal about agent harnesses and called contests a valuable learning opportunity. The post links the current Kaggle competition.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A first-person ARC-3 engineering account, now connected through the direct Kaggle profile link to team 16992721. It is an attributed experience, not a claimed cause of any score.

socialPosts.author: mikeknoop
socialPosts.summary: Mike Knoop said the same thing is happening with ARC-AGI-3 while quoting Pedro Domingos’s comment that models are absorbing harness behavior. The quoted post links Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation. Knoop gives no named team, method, score or ARC experiment. The linked paper trains a proposer to revise executable harness code using feedback; its reported evaluations cover reasoning and multi-hop question answering, so the ARC-3 observation remains Knoop’s attributed comment.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Fresh ARC co-founder reaction for reporting on how models and harnesses divide the work. Useful research context, with no new verified Kaggle result or evidence that harnesses disappear.

socialPosts.author: Fei2411
socialPosts.summary: FeiZ reported a one-level ls20 ARC-AGI-3 comparison: a DS Bot cleared that level within 81 steps, while a DeepSeek Harness exhausted 110 steps without clearing it. This is the author’s own small test, not a Kaggle standing or verified benchmark result.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Recent ARC-AGI-3 community experiment; the author explicitly says one level proves little.
